meta.title: WorkGuardAI: measured groundwork progress from your DWG plan
meta.description: WorkGuardAI reads the DWG plan you already have and measures groundwork and infrastructure progress from ordinary site photos, location by location. Working prototype, looking for the first pilot site.
hero.h1: From DWG plan to measured progress.
hero.lead: WorkGuardAI reads the DWG plan you already have and measures groundwork progress from ordinary site photos, location by location. The prototype works on a real project's plan and imagery. Now we are looking for the first pilot site.
hero.alt: Open excavation with a sloped earth wall and a sandy floor.
hero.caption: Illustrative overlay on an excavation photo. Local grid, not real site coordinates.
how.h2: From a DWG plan and ordinary photos to progress at each location.
how.s1a: A drone and cameras photographing an excavation
how.s1d: Ordinary site photos from a phone, camera or drone, taken at coordinates from your plan. No special hardware.
how.s2a: Points from the DWG plan with newly changed areas highlighted
how.s2d: Each new photo is measured for pixel and colour change at its plan coordinate.
how.s3a: Detected excavation compared with the planned DWG profile, 62 percent complete (sample data)
how.s3d: Progress is compared automatically with the DWG plan the contractor already has.
how.s4a: A dashboard showing progress and an alert when work deviates from plan (sample data)
how.s4d: Progress updates per coordinate, with email alerts on progress, stalls and deviations.
how.note: Illustrative concept with sample data. Working prototype; field test pending. Exploring next: camera GPS and LiDAR for higher precision.
proto.h2: Built on a real project's plan and imagery.
proto.lead: The prototype has been demonstrated on a real DWG file and real site photos. It has not yet run on a live site. The first field test is the next step.
proto.note: Prototype interface, tested on a real project's plan and imagery. Field test next.
how.fieldP: Ordinary site photos, like the ones the prototype measures: taken by phone or drone, by day and at night.

proto.today1: Reads the DWG plan and builds a coordinate map of the site.
proto.today2: Measures pixel and colour change in site photos taken at plan coordinates.
proto.today4: Sends email alerts on progress, stalls and deviations.
proto.next1: A field test on a live site, with a contractor or infrastructure owner.
proto.next2: Camera GPS combined with LiDAR, to place photos and measure depth more precisely.
proto.next3: Integrations with the tools site teams already use.
for.h2: For the people who build and own the groundwork.
for.c_p: You already have the DWG plan. WorkGuardAI uses it to show how far excavation and groundwork have come at each location, from photos your team can take on a normal site visit.
for.o_p: Cities and agencies that commission roads, utilities and public works can follow progress per location against the approved plan, measured from site photos.

pilot.lead: We are looking for the first live site. If you run groundwork or infrastructure work and have DWG plans for it, a short call is enough to see whether a pilot fits.
pilot.s1p: We show the prototype on a demo project and check that your site fits: groundwork or infrastructure, DWG plans, and someone who can take photos.
pilot.s2p: One site, a fixed period and clear data handling, agreed in a short pilot agreement. We load your DWG plan and set up access for your team.
pilot.s3p: Your team takes photos at plan coordinates. We check in every week and compare the results with your own measurements. You get a written results report.
pilot.pricing: Pilots are agreed one site at a time. Pricing is set after the field test, based on what it shows.
partner.p: For technology, surveying and construction partners, and for funding bodies, cities, universities and investors who back early European construction technology.

privacy.title: Privacy notice · WorkGuardAI
privacy.metaDesc: How WorkGuardAI handles the personal data you send through the pilot call form or by email.
privacy.intro: This notice explains what personal data we receive through this website, why, and what rights you have. We collect as little as possible.
privacy.whoP: WorkGuardAI is the controller of the personal data described here.
privacy.collectP1: When you send the pilot call form: your name, company, role, type of site, whether you have DWG plans, email address and your message. When you email us: what you write and your email address.
privacy.collectP2: This website uses no cookies, no analytics and no tracking. Fonts and images are served from this site, not from third parties.
privacy.whyP: Only to reply to your request and to discuss a possible pilot with you. The legal basis is taking steps at your request before a possible agreement (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)) and our legitimate interest in answering business enquiries (Article 6(1)(f)).
privacy.procFormspree: Formspree, Inc. (United States) receives the form and delivers it to our email. Your data is transferred to the United States for this; Formspree's privacy policy states that it makes such transfers as permitted by law and keeps the data appropriately protected.
privacy.procEmail: Google Workspace provides our email and stores the messages we receive.
privacy.procHosting: GitHub, Inc. hosts this website. Like any web server, it may log technical data such as IP addresses for security.
privacy.procNoSale: We do not sell your data or share it with anyone else.
privacy.keepP: We copy each request into our own records and then delete it from Formspree. If a request does not lead to a pilot or other cooperation, we delete it no later than 12 months after our last contact.
privacy.rightsP: You can ask to see the data we hold about you, to correct or delete it, to restrict or object to its use, or to receive it in a portable format. Write to ek@workguardai.com and we will reply within one month.
privacy.complaintP: You can also complain to a data protection authority. In Finland this is the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman (tietosuoja.fi); you can also contact the authority in your own country.
privacy.changesP: If we change how we handle personal data, we will update this page and the date above.
